best_for: People who need to trim ads out of a recording, cut a clip from a long video or re-encode a file to another format, and do not want to learn a full video editor to do it.

points.title: Cut, filter, encode
points.text: Avidemux is built for simple jobs: cutting out sections, applying filters and re-encoding. It reads common containers such as AVI, MP4, DVD-style MPEG and ASF. Projects, a job queue and scripting let you repeat the same job on many files.

points.title: Copy mode is fast but cuts on keyframes
points.text: With the video output left on Copy, Avidemux saves without re-encoding, so it is quick and keeps full quality. The catch is that each cut must start on a keyframe, or the file breaks at the cut. Frame-exact cuts need a real encoder, which is slower and loses some quality.

points.title: Releases are slow
points.text: The current stable release, 2.8.1, dates from September 2022. Newer fixes appear only in the project's nightly builds. The Windows listing here keeps just 2 versions.

points.title: Mac install has a snag
points.text: The macOS download is a single universal .dmg. Homebrew disabled its Avidemux cask on 2026-09-01 because the app fails Apple's Gatekeeper check, so macOS may refuse to open it until you allow it yourself.

points.title: Linux: AppImage or community Flatpak
points.text: The project itself offers a 64-bit AppImage, a legacy AppImage for older systems and source code. The Flatpak listed here is a Flathub build for x64 and Arm64 that Flathub does not mark as verified. macOS and Linux list only the current release.

points.title: Free and GPL
points.text: Avidemux is free under the GNU GPL. The download page says the Windows installer carries no bundled toolbars or other extras.
